Report: MindsEye developer Build a Rocket Boy seemingly closing after more layoffs
Multiple staff on the studio have written farewell posts on social media over the past 24 hours.
Diego Argüello
,
Contributing Editor, News
,
GameDeveloper.com
September 16, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
Image via Build a Rocket Boy
Build a Rocket Boy (BARB), the studio behind
MindsEye
, is reportedly winding down operations, as alleged by multiple farewell posts from staff via social media.
Over at LinkedIn, developers at the studio have spent the last 24 hours announcing their departures. The person in charge of principal talent acquisition partner and HR operations
said
that they're raising their green banner, referring to the #OpenForWork image tag, along with the rest of his colleagues.
"Just shy of 5 years here at BARB and one hell of a ride! Being the first hire into our internal recruitment team, taking the studio from 200 to 550 in a short period of time," the developer wrote.
In addition, they add they'll be "seeing BARB through till the very end, helping wrap things up" in the HR department.
The lead 3D weapon/prop artist
repeated the same phrase
as their colleague. "Unfortunately, along with the rest of my colleagues at Build a Rocket Boy, I am facing redundancy and now looking for a new opportunity."
Related:
Shinji Mikami to join AIAS Hall of Fame at 2026 DICE Awards
Then, a Technical Level Designer (UGC) at the studio
echoed the messaging
: "Hi everyone, much like others at BARB, I find myself once again raising the green banner looking for new opportunities."
Kotaku reports
that sources familiar with the situation have told the publication that Build a Rocket Boy is permanently closing its doors. The studio is yet to acknowledge the reported layoffs or closure.
The studio has had a tumultuous run during the development of
MindsEye
, as well as the time since its June 2025 launch. Almost 100 developers
signed an open letter
containing allegations of debilitating mismanagement, with some even filing legal claims. The team was hit by multiple rounds of job cuts while Build a Rocket Boy claimed the troubled launch was due to "
corporate sabotage
."
Then, IOI Partners, a division of Hitman developer IO Interactive,
stepped down
as publisher of
MindsEye
early this year. In while, game workers
protested alleged misconduct outside the Edinburgh office
of the developer, following legal action from the IWGB Game Workers Union over allegations of data privacy violations related to the installation of surveillance software on work devices.
Game Developer has contacted Build a Rocket Boy for corroboration.
